__comment: The Park Bulletin (/now). One file per NPS Yosemite Guide edition. When the park publishes a new Guide (roughly every five weeks), rewrite this file from it, then (1) bump the shared ?v= on BULLETIN_URL (page-now.jsx) and TIOGA_BULLETIN_URL (page-tioga-opening.jsx), (2) run `npm --prefix scripts run compile`, `npm --prefix scripts run seo` and `npm --prefix scripts run assets:stamp`, (3) commit. `node scripts/check-bulletin.mjs` (part of `npm --prefix scripts run check`) validates every field named here. Facts come from the printed Guide plus park sources; a row the Guide does not carry is a row this file does not carry. Every date is ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) and the page reads it against today's date in Yosemite, so nothing here is written relative to a day ('tomorrow', 'this week'): the page works that out, which is what lets one file stay correct for five weeks. FIELDS. edition: label, start, end, updated (drives the /now sitemap lastmod and the deploy-parity stamp), lede (original house copy, no em-dashes), source, sourceUrl, and an optional notice, one sentence shown above everything (the stale-edition note goes here). headlines: two to four tiles carrying the edition's most important facts, { label, icon, status, tone, text }; tone is open | warn | closed; icon is a BULLETIN_ICONS name from page-now.jsx, optional, and restates what the text already says, never a new fact (an unknown name renders the neutral mark). changes: the dated ledger the page splits at today into 'Coming up' and 'Already closed', { date, when, kind, what, detail }. kind is closes | ends | hours | opens | event. date is the date the Guide gives: on and before it the row is coming up, after it the row has happened (a past closes or ends row lists under 'Already closed', a past hours row under 'Hours changed', and a past opens or event row drops off, because the schedule carries it). when is an optional display label that replaces the date ('Early October', with date set to the day it sorts by); a row with no date is season-long and when names its group ('This season', 'Out of order'). areas: { name, chip, tone, note }, read by /now, by /tioga-opening (the Tioga row) and by the crawler prose. programAreas: the schedule's tabs, { key, name, short, notes }, notes being [{ h, t }] for the area's standing extras that are not a timed row. programs: every timed program and dated event in the Guide, { area, time, title, detail, detailByDay, where, days, from, until, dates, except, fee, access, allAges, tag }. area is a programAreas key, or 'parkwide' for a park-wide event, which shows above every area's list and may omit time. time is the Guide's start time ('9:00 am', 'Noon'). days is 'daily' or a list of su mo tu we th fr sa. from and until bound a run, inclusive. dates lists the exact days of a one-off or scattered event and replaces days; except removes single dates. detailByDay maps a day code to that day's detail. fee marks a paid, ticketed or registered-and-paid row. access and allAges are the printed Guide's own per-program symbols (wheelchair accessible, recommended for families), read off the Programs page row by row and true-only, because an unmarked program is one the Guide did not mark rather than one it ruled out. The same two marks ride the PWA's program feed as accessible / familyFriendly (workers/src/data/manual-programs.ts); re-read both from the new Programs page every edition. tag is an optional short label ('Exhibit', 'Last of the season'); one-day rows are labelled by the page. programsNote: the schedule's footnote. trails: { name, chip, tone, distance, start, note }; open rows list under 'Open as usual', warn and closed rows under 'Check before you go'. hours: groups of { name, hours, note, closes, then }; closes is the last open day, after which the row reads Closed, and then is { from, hours }, the hours from that date on. transit: { name, note, until }, until being the last day a seasonal service runs. essentials: { title, text }. numbers: { label, value }.

edition.label: September 23 – November 24, 2026
edition.lede: The edition where the park packs up for winter. The Tuolumne visitor center shuts Sep 27, the wilderness permit desks by Oct 18, the Glacier Point tour bus on Oct 11 and most of the Valley's seasonal counters on Oct 25. Overnight parking on Tioga and Glacier Point Roads ends Oct 15, and both roads usually close for the season sometime in November, on the weather's schedule rather than the calendar's. The Valley stays open and gets quieter: the falls are dry, the oaks are turning, and the rangers are still walking.
edition.source: Condensed from the National Park Service Yosemite Guide for September 23 – November 24, 2026, with the park's current conditions page and the journal's own notes.

headlines.label: High roads
headlines.text: Tioga and Glacier Point Roads usually close for the winter sometime in November. No overnight parking on either from Oct 15. When Tioga closes there is no way through to Highway 395. Road status: 209/372-0200, press 1 then 1.

areas.name: Yosemite Valley
areas.note: Quieter than summer, but parking can still fill by late morning on weekends and holidays. Park once in one of the three hubs, Curry Village, Yosemite Village, or Yosemite Falls, and walk, bike, or ride the free shuttle. El Capitan Bridge work means 15-minute delays Monday to Friday, 7 am to 7 pm, through December; shuttle stop 9 is closed and the footpath over the bridge is shut on weekdays.

areas.name: Tioga Road & Tuolumne Meadows
areas.note: Very few or no services in the fall: the store, grill, lodge, and buses are done, the visitor center closes Sep 27 and the wilderness center Oct 14. No overnight parking from Oct 15. The road typically closes for winter sometime in November, and when it does there is no access to or from the east side. Construction delays of 10 minutes through the meadows and 15 minutes from Olmsted Point to Tioga Pass, 8 am to 3:30 pm Monday to Thursday. The trail between the wilderness center and Lembert Dome is closed for construction, with an alternate signed.

areas.name: Glacier Point Road
areas.note: One hour from the Valley. The gift shop runs 9 am to 7 pm through Oct 25, the tour bus through Oct 11, and there is no overnight parking from Oct 15. The road typically closes for winter in November. The Ostrander Lake Trail and everything south of it are closed for the Dome Fire. No trailers or vehicles over 30 feet past the Sentinel Dome trailhead.

areas.name: Wawona & Mariposa Grove
areas.note: An hour south of the Valley. Free grove shuttle every 15 minutes, 8 am to 5 pm through Oct 31 (last bus down 5:30), then 8 am to 3:30 pm in November. The visitor center closes Oct 31 and its permit desk Oct 14. The Dome Fire is burning northeast of Wawona: the Chilnualna Falls trail and the trails above it are closed. The hotel is closed for renovation.

areas.name: Crane Flat
areas.note: Thirty minutes up Big Oak Flat Road, and the quiet way to see sequoias: Tuolumne Grove 2 miles round trip, Merced Grove 3. Information station 8 am to 5 pm, 9 am from Oct 19; permit pickup through Oct 18. The store closes Oct 25; the pumps stay open. Weekday delays of about 15 minutes on Big Oak Flat Road between Foresta and Crane Flat for forest thinning.

areas.name: Hetch Hetchy
areas.note: An hour and a half from the Valley, with no services. From Oct 19, self-register for wilderness permits at the entrance kiosk. No vehicles or trailers over 25 feet long or 8 feet wide on the entrance road, no swimming or boating, and no pets on the dam or the trails.

areas.name: Gas
areas.note: El Portal 15 miles downhill on 140, Crane Flat 16.5 miles uphill on Big Oak Flat Road, Wawona 28 miles up Wawona Road. All pump 24 hours with a card.

programsNote: Everything unmarked is free and drop-in. The accessible and all-ages marks are the Yosemite Guide's own symbols: accessible means the program is held in a wheelchair-accessible facility or uses wheelchair-accessible paths, and the park asks you to raise any other accommodation with the program host. An unmarked program is one the Guide did not mark, not one it ruled out. The schedule is subject to change, and the park posts additions at go.nps.gov/YosemiteCalendar.

trails.name: Mist Trail to Vernal & Nevada Falls
trails.distance: Footbridge 1.6 mi, 380 ft · top of Vernal 2.4 mi, 1,000 ft · top of Nevada 5 mi, 2,000 ft
trails.note: Closed M – Th, 7 am – 3:30 pm for repairs through the end of October; open F – Su, holidays, and outside those hours when conditions allow. Use the signed John Muir Trail detour during the closure. Looping back on the John Muir Trail by Clark Point makes Vernal 3.7 miles and Nevada 5.8. In November the park may close the Mist Trail above the footbridge, and the John Muir Trail between Clark Point and the Panorama junction, for winter.

trails.name: Chilnualna Falls
trails.note: Closed for the Dome Fire, along with the trails from the top toward Buena Vista and Crescent Lakes, which are still reachable from the east. No reopening date announced.

trails.name: Ostrander Lake
trails.note: The trail and every area and trail south of it are closed for the Dome Fire. The closure runs east of Wawona Road from Chinquapin to Wawona; the park's public information map shows the line.

trails.name: Half Dome
trails.note: A permit every day while the cables are up, which the Guide puts at late May to early October. Daily lottery two days ahead on Recreation.gov. Days are short now: start in the dark with a headlamp.

trails.name: Lower Yosemite Fall
trails.note: East side wheelchair-accessible. The fall is dry until the storms return. Go for the amphitheater and the scale of the wall.

trails.name: Mirror Lake
trails.distance: 2 mi, 100 ft on the paved road · 4.5 mi around the basin
trails.note: The lakebed is a meadow this time of year. Leashed pets on the paved road only; a valid disability placard may drive it.

trails.name: Bridalveil Fall
trails.note: Paved to a wheelchair-accessible viewing area, steeper to the base. The fall is low this time of year. Stay behind the barriers: the rocks at the base are slick.

trails.name: Cook's Meadow
trails.note: Pavement and boardwalk. Half Dome and Yosemite Falls views, with the oaks turning; the birds are out early and around dusk.

trails.name: Yosemite Falls Trail
trails.distance: Columbia Rock 2 mi · the top 7.2 mi, 2,700 ft
trails.note: Columbia Rock earns the view. The full climb is six to eight hours and dozens of switchbacks to a dry fall: start early, because the light goes sooner now.

trails.name: Four Mile Trail
trails.note: To Glacier Point, six to eight hours. Through Oct 11 you can ride the tour bus up and walk down; drop-offs only, no pickup at the point. The upper portion closes in winter.

trails.name: Valley Loop Trail
trails.note: Mostly flat but uneven, and the quietest miles on the floor. The El Capitan Bridge crossing is closed on weekdays through December for bridge work, so on a weekday walk the north and south sides as two out-and-backs, or come on a weekend for the full loop. No pets or bikes.

trails.name: Sentinel Dome & Taft Point
trails.distance: Taft Point 2.4 mi · Sentinel Dome 1.8 mi
trails.note: One trailhead, two rim walks: Taft Point to the west, Sentinel Dome to the northeast. Reachable until Glacier Point Road closes for winter, typically in November.

trails.name: Lembert Dome
trails.note: The trail between the wilderness center and Lembert Dome is closed for construction; an alternate trail is signed.

trails.name: Tuolumne & Merced Groves
trails.distance: Tuolumne 2 mi, 500 ft · Merced 3 mi, 520 ft
trails.note: The uncrowded sequoias. You walk down first, so save the legs for the return. Rangers lead the Tuolumne Grove hike M, W, and Th at 1 pm through Nov 1.

trailsNote: Overnights require a wilderness permit year-round, and a bear canister. The permit desks close in mid-October: Tuolumne and Wawona pickup Oct 14, the Valley and Big Oak Flat Oct 18. After that, self-register outside the Valley Welcome Center, on the Wawona, Big Oak Flat, or Tuolumne porch, or at the Hetch Hetchy entrance kiosk from Oct 19, each for its own trailheads only, and rent canisters only at the Valley Welcome Center. Carry a quart of water per person for every two hours, a headlamp, a map, and warm, waterproof layers; expect winter trail conditions by November. Turn around when half the water is gone. No pets or bikes on any hiking trail. Big-wall climbers self-register for overnight permits at the kiosk near shuttle stop 9.

transit.name: Valley shuttles
transit.note: Free, daily 7 am – 10 pm, year-round. Valleywide green line hits every stop, every 22 – 32 minutes, an hour and a half round trip; the purple East Valley line runs every 18 – 22 minutes, 50 minutes round trip. Stop 9, El Capitan Meadow, is closed. No pets.

transit.note: Free, every 15 minutes, no ticket. Sep 23, 8 am – 7 pm; Sep 24 to Oct 31, 8 am – 5 pm with the last bus down at 5:30; November, 8 am – 3:30 pm with the last bus down at 5.

transit.name: Glacier Point tour bus
transit.note: Four hours from Yosemite Valley Lodge at 8:30 am and 1:30 pm, paid, at TravelYosemite.com or the Lodge front desk. One-way hiker tickets drop off only; no pickup at the point.

transit.name: Tuolumne buses
transit.note: The hikers bus and the Tuolumne Meadows shuttle are summer-only and have ended. The high country is drive-yourself until Tioga Road closes.

transit.name: YARTS
transit.note: Public transit into the park. Merced (Highway 140) runs year-round with multiple departures. The Fresno (Highway 41) route runs through Sep 25 and the Sonora (Highway 120) and Mammoth Lakes (395) routes through Sep 30, then stop for the season. YARTS.com or 877/989-2787.

transit.name: Bikes
transit.note: Over 11 miles of paved path on the Valley floor, 15 mph limit, helmets required under 18, no bikes on hiking trails. E-bikes under 750 watts with working pedals go wherever bikes go. Rentals 9 am – 6 pm, 9 am – 5 pm from Sep 28, through Oct 25 when conditions allow; adaptive bikes, scooters, and wheelchairs at 209/372-1208. Free bike share for one- to two-hour rides from the Village and Camp 4 lots until late October, goyose.org/bikeshare.

essentials.title: Bears
essentials.text: Food storage is federal law: within arm's reach by day, out of the car and into a locker by night, and never in a truck bed or strapped to the outside. To a bear, food means anything with a scent, trash and toiletries included. Twenty-seven bears were hit by vehicles here last year, so hold the speed limit at dawn and dusk. Sightings: 209/372-0322 or yose_bear_mgmt@nps.gov.

essentials.title: Chains
essentials.text: Expect chain restrictions on park roads from November to March, especially during and after storms. When they are in effect every vehicle must carry chains, four-wheel drive and rentals included. Storms are possible from late October: call 209/372-0200, press 1 then 1, before you drive, and see go.nps.gov/chains.

essentials.title: Smoke & fire
essentials.text: Fire season runs into the fall, and the Dome Fire is still burning near Wawona. Check air quality at fire.airnow.gov the morning you drive in. Fires only in portable stoves, grills, and established rings, never unattended, and out cold before you walk away. More restrictions may apply.

essentials.title: Short days
essentials.text: The light goes early and the nights are cold, especially up high. Pack a headlamp and warm, waterproof layers, finish before dark, and expect winter trail conditions by November. Stay off domes when lightning is possible.

essentials.title: Wildlife
essentials.text: 150 feet from bears and coyotes, 25 feet from everything else. Feeding or approaching any animal is illegal, birds and squirrels included.

essentials.title: Camping
essentials.text: Until Oct 26 every campground needs a reservation: Recreation.gov or 877/444-6777. After that, Wawona and Hodgdon Meadow go first-come, first-served, Upper Pines stays reservation-only year-round, and Camp 4 through Nov 9; the rest close in September and October. Sleeping in a vehicle is legal only at a registered site.

essentials.title: Parking
essentials.text: Designated spaces or paved turnouts only, pulled fully off the road. Vehicles on vegetation get cited and towed. No overnight parking on Tioga or Glacier Point Roads from Oct 15.

essentials.title: Pets
essentials.text: Not allowed on trails, on shuttles, or inside buildings. Leashed on paved roads, paved bike paths, and the Mirror Lake road. Service dogs go anywhere visitors go; emotional support and therapy animals follow the pet rules.

essentials.title: The rules with teeth
essentials.text: Prohibited: drones, feeding or approaching wildlife, collecting plants, animals, or arrowheads, hunting, metal detectors, driving into meadows, biking off pavement, camping outside a designated campground, weapons inside federal buildings, and marijuana of any kind.

essentials.title: Navigation
essentials.text: GPS gives wrong directions inside the park and routes people onto closed roads. Follow the road signs. There is no usable signal for most of Tioga Road or Glacier Point Road.

essentials.title: Wifi
essentials.text: Free at Degnan's Kitchen and the Mariposa County Library in the Valley, the El Portal Market, and the Wawona library. Hotel guests get it at the Lodge, Curry Village, and The Ahwahnee.
